auditFix.issue: Card commits primary gloss to '갈다 = to grind' (Wiktionary Etymology 2: 칼을 갈다, 맷돌에 갈다). The sentence '낡은 신발을 새것으로 갈았어요' demonstrates the homonym '갈다 = to replace/swap/change' (Wiktionary Etymology 1: 옷을 갈아입다, 부품을 갈다). These are distinct etymologies — different historical origins, same modern form. The 'to change' sense is acknowledged in senses[] but the sentence should illustrate the committed primary 'to grind'.

evidence.note: Wiktionary lists 갈다 as having three distinct etymologies: Etymology 1 = to change/replace/switch (1447), Etymology 2 = to grind/whet/sharpen (1459), Etymology 3 = to plow. The committed primary 'to grind' is Etymology 2; the sentence uses Etymology 1.

auditFix.suggestion: Replace with a sentence using the primary 'to grind/sharpen' sense, e.g. '대장장이가 칼을 갈고 있어요.' ('The blacksmith is sharpening a knife.') or '맷돌에 콩을 갈았어요.' ('I ground beans on the millstone.').

auditFix.issue: Target lemma is 트다 (active/transitive: 'to crack, to clear, to open [a passage]', e.g. 입술이 트다, 거래선을 트다). The form 트인 in the sentence is the attributive past of the passive/intransitive 트이다, not 트다. The collocation 탁 트인 들판 is real and natural, but it exemplifies 트이다, not the lemma 트다. Wrong-lemma mismatch (parallel to the entry-30 나다 vs 떠나다 case the prior auditor caught).

evidence.note: Wiktionary lists 쓰다 with four distinct etymologies: 1=to wear, 2=to write, 3=to use, 4=to be bitter (explicitly classed as adjective, separate from the verb etymologies). The committed primary 'to write' is Etymology 2 (verb); the sentence uses Etymology 4 (adjective).

auditFix.issue: Card commits primary gloss to '이상 = abnormal' (異常). The sentence '그 이상은 묻지 마세요' uses '이상 = above / more than' (以上). These are distinct Sino-Korean homonyms with different hanja and different meanings — 異常 ('strange/abnormal') vs 以上 ('an amount more than or equal to'). The 'above' sense is acknowledged in senses[] but the sentence should illustrate the committed primary 異常.

evidence.note: Wiktionary lists three distinct Sino-Korean homonyms: 以上 (more than/above, noun), 異常 (strange/abnormal, adjective), 理想 (ideal, noun). Same pronunciation 이상, different hanja, different meanings. The committed primary 'abnormal' is 異常; the sentence uses 以上.

auditFix.suggestion: Replace with a sentence using the primary 異常 ('abnormal') sense, e.g. '포켓몬의 상태에 이상이 있어요.' ('There is something abnormal about the Pokémon's condition.') or '기계에 이상이 생겼어요.' ('Something went wrong with the machine.').

auditFix.issue: Card commits primary gloss to '슬다 = to lay (eggs)' (used of insects/fish depositing eggs, e.g. 알을 슬다). The sentence '녹이 슨 자전거를 닦아요' uses '슬다 = to rust / form (mold)' (쇠붙이에 녹이 생기다 — for rust/mold to develop on metal). The 'to rust' sense is acknowledged in senses[] but the sentence should illustrate the committed primary 'to lay (eggs)'.

evidence.note: Standard Korean Learner's Dictionary (krdict, NIKL) records 슬다 with the rust/mold-forming sense ('쇠붙이에 녹이 생기다'); the egg-laying sense ('벌레나 물고기가 알을 깔기어 놓다', e.g. 알을 슬다) is the basic native sense recorded in 표준국어대사전. Committed primary is egg-laying; sentence demonstrates the rust sense.

auditFix.suggestion: Replace with a sentence using the primary 'to lay (eggs)' sense, e.g. '메뚜기가 풀잎에 알을 슬었어요.' ('The grasshopper laid eggs on the blade of grass.') or '연어가 강에서 알을 슬어요.' ('Salmon lay eggs in the river.').
auditFix.reviewerNote: Rejected auditor's generic grasshopper; use a Pokémon egg-laying reference. Butterfree (Bug-type) keeps 슬다 in its insect/fish egg-laying register.

auditFix.issue: 전광석화 (電光石火) is a four-character idiom whose lexical meaning is 'as fast as lightning/flint sparks' — speed is baked into the word. Adding the adverb 재빨리 ('quickly') immediately after produces tautological reinforcement: literally 'charged lightning-fast quickly'. auditFix.issue: The official Korean move name 껍질에숨기 contains the internal locative particle 에 ('hide IN [the] shell'). When followed by the object marker 를, learners parse the string as '...껍질에 숨기를...' (two competing clausal readings: '...is in shell, learning to hide...' vs '...is learning [the move] Withdraw'). The double-particle stacking inside a single noun phrase is awkward Korean and causes ambiguity for L2 readers. The previous auditor flagged this as 'uncertain' and no fix was applied; the issue persists.

auditFix.issue: 발버둥 (Struggle) is the auto-triggered fallback move that fires only when a Pokémon has no PP left on any other move. A trainer cannot deliberately '사용하다' Struggle, so '체육관 시합에서 발버둥을 사용했어요' frames an automatic, last-resort move as a chosen tactic. The Korean is grammatical (and 발버둥 also has the everyday meaning 'thrashing/floundering', which makes it superficially read fine), but the in-game collocation is semantically off and atypical of how Korean Pokémon discourse describes Struggle (one would say 발버둥을 쳤어요 / 발버둥치게 됐어요, not 발버둥을 사용했어요).
